I realize you are upset however you need to get more information before playing the blame game. Call the local fire department and find out what their average response time is for your area, they will have this. This will tell you what you should have expected. If they took longer than expected ask why. Perhaps they were at a car accident or another fire on the other side of town. Thirdly as mentioned by someone else see if they are a volunteer fire department. Those types of departments have to wait for the volunteers to get to the truck before they drive to your house. The town I live in was all volunteer up till the 80's. The running joke was our Fire Department saves another foundation.

About the fire itself. A short in a wall is an extremely rare occurrence. Think about it. The wires are protected by the wall itself and the insulation of the wires. In order for them to short out they have to be damaged somehow. That's really hard to do. Most fires are easily preventable. Were animals allowed to live in the walls? Were there too many things plugged into the outlets on that particular circuit? Were the circuit breakers or fuses in working order and not over ridden? Was the outlet cover actually there on the outlet? Was there obvious damage to the wiring? ie. holes in the walls improper splicing or adding additional circuits. All of the previous issues cost zero dollars to fix. Did they have a fire extinguisher in the kitchen and did they use it? Most fire departments will give you a kitchen fire extinguisher if you ask. I know it's been mentioned before but homeowners insurance is the cheapest safety net to buy.
